published_figures.source: DoD Selected Acquisition Report, F-22, December 2010; USAF F-22 fact sheet
published_figures.figure: The report's supercruise, "Vmax/Opt Alt/Mil Power": Mach 1.76, demonstrated, at military power, 0.99, and the best altitude - flown level at every 2,000 ft from 30,000 to 50,000 ft, the fastest.
The report's acceleration, "Acceleration/.8-1.5/30K": 52.4 seconds, demonstrated, from Mach 0.8 to 1.5 at 30,000 ft, at maximum power.

The report's manoeuvrability, "max power sustained G", at 30,000 ft and Mach 0.9: 3.7 g, demonstrated - a turn rate of 7.34 degrees a second, g times the root of n squared less one, over the true airspeed, 895 ft/s. The tolerance takes in the report's objective, 3.9 g.

The fact sheet's speed, "mach two class": level at 40,000 ft at full throttle it reaches Mach 2, within the class this project reads as 1.95 to 2.35. Lockheed Martin (18 November 2002) had it cleared to Mach 2.
The fact sheet's ceiling, "above 50,000 feet": at 50,000 ft, at maximum power, it still climbs at 100 ft/min, the rate that makes a service ceiling.
